newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks expected to trade sideways.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks expected to trade sideways.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were expected to trade sideways on Monday ahead of more economic figures from the United States which might provide clues on inflation and give the market some direction, brokers said.
"In the short term, the market will trade in a narrow range, waiting for more economic data from the U.S," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 35.59 points at 12,610.17 on Monday. On Wall Street, the Dow industrials closed higher overnight after a three-session losing streak, rising 44.15 points to 6,783.02.
The Hang Seng London Reference index rose 22.43 points, or 0.18 percent, overnight to 12,632.60.
Edwin Cheung, dealing director with Taiwan Securities, said the market would move sideways, with selling pressures undermining any gains in the morning session.
Brokers expected some consolidation in red chips, and said the April futures contract, which expires later Tuesday, to trade around 12,600.
U.S. first quarter employment cost index data, a closely watched barometer of wage inflation, is due out on Tuesday, and April employment data is released on Friday.
